name: Tact
overview: The Scriptures demonstrate that tact involves wise and measured responses to conflict and opposition, as seen when Gideon calms the anger of the men of Ephraim by respectfully comparing their contributions (Judges 8:1-3). Saul's silence in the face of insult from the children of Belial (1 Samuel 10:27) and his decisive yet strategic actions in rallying Israel against their enemies (1 Samuel 11:7) further illustrate the prudent use of restraint and firm leadership. These examples reveal that tact in biblical leadership balances courage with sensitivity to human emotions and the need for unity.
